author: Forbes
description:
China’s enthusiasm for new stocks has helped to mint two billionaires on paper, as the surging shares of tape maker Crown New Materials Technology during its trading debut on Tuesday have made its Chairman and CEO, former elementary school teacher Mai Michael, and his sister immensely rich.

Mai, 62, who now has Australian citizenship and is a permanent resident of Hong Kong, has a net worth of $2.5 billion based on his stake, according to Forbes estimates. His sister, Mai Huixia, 64, a Chinese citizen and the company’s vice chairman, has amassed a $2 billion fortune from her stake, according to Forbes. The company didn’t respond to a request for comment on their net worth.

author: Forbes
description:
In New York City, floodwaters can rise three to four feet in just 20 minutes, often before emergency responders even know where flooding is happening.

FloodNet NYC is working to change that. With a network of 450 sensors across the city, the project tracks flooding in real time, giving officials critical information to improve emergency response and help communities prepare.

But can a city ever truly be disaster-proof? FloodNet's researchers explain how real-time data could transform the way cities respond to flooding and prepare for an increasingly unpredictable future.

author: Forbes
description:
Are robot butlers finally becoming a reality, or is the future of consumer tech still more hype than innovation?

Forbes Vetted executive editor and resident robotics expert Dave Johnson traveled to Berlin, Germany, for IFA 2026, one of the world's largest consumer technology shows, to find out what's actually next in tech. From stair-climbing robot vacuums and AI-powered gadgets to robotic lawnmowers, wearable exoskeletons and futuristic diving gear, Dave goes hands-on with some of the most interesting innovations on the show floor.

But with companies promising humanoid robots that can cook, clean and tackle everyday chores, one big question remains: How close are we really to having robots in our homes?

Join Dave as he separates the hype from reality and explores the technology that could change how we live.
